target_customer: Nigerian salaried consumers and shoppers who want credit to buy goods and services, and merchants who sell to them
problem: Few Nigerians have access to credit cards or consumer credit, so large purchases require cash upfront.
business_model: Buy now pay later consumer credit with merchant fees and interest

founders.name: Fehintolu Olaogun
founders.background_notes: Named CEO in the December 2020 Fintech Global article; the YC page lists the founder as Mofehintolu Olaogun.

founders.name: Olorunfemi Jegede
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in the Fintech Global article (2020-12); COO per Technext search listing.

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit scoring, repayment collection and merchant integrations in a market with thin credit data; standard fintech engineering with underwriting risk as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: BNPL lending is replicable by banks and fintechs; advantages depend on underwriting data and funding access.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Jumia offered BNPL from 2015 per search coverage; later entrants such as Carbon launched BNPL in 2021 while CredPal kept operating.

market_need_then: The 2020 article describes a goal of an American Express of Africa, reflecting the lack of credit cards and consumer credit in Nigeria.

brand_strength.rationale: Credit plus pal reads clearly, but no brand coverage was found and the name resembles other credit brands.

outcome_analysis: CredPal raised a 1.5 million dollar round in December 2020 and a 15 million dollar debt and equity package in March 2022 to expand BNPL across Africa, and remains active with about 35 staff. Its progress depends on lending capital and credit quality in Nigeria, but no later round, shutdown or sizable growth data was found in sources.
notes: The 2022 round is stated as debt and equity by Nairametrics, The Condia, Tech Gist Africa and the YC page; CB Insights labels it Series A while Caplight lists debt, so stage is other and the equity versus debt split is unknown. Investors for 2022 come from CB Insights via a search listing. Total raised ranges 16.5M to 19.7M across aggregators and is not used. The 2020 article was not read for 2017 versus 2018 founding; YC lists 2018 and the article says launched 2017. No competitor source dated near 2019 was found; Jumia BNPL (2015) appeared only in a later search snippet. No layoff or shutdown news found.
